newsitem.title: USA: Harris County $125 mln TANS bid at 3.77 pct.
newsitem.headline: Harris County $125 mln TANS bid at 3.77 pct.

text.p: A syndicate led by Zions First National Bank Capital Markets submitted the lowest bid of 3.77 percent for sale of Harris County's $125 million tax anticipation notes (TANS), a county spokesman said.

Of the 13 bids received Tuesday, the Zions First National group's offer came in at 3.77 percent, said Terry Thornton, assistant director of financial services for the county where Houston is located. The highest bid quoted an interest rate of 3.85 percent, he said.
The notes will mature on Feb. 27, 1998, the end of the county's fiscal year.

TANS are short-term borrowings used by municipal governments to finance current expenditures pending receipt of expected tax payments. TANS even out cash flow and are repaid when the tax revenues are received.
